subject: Bridging support: Gatekeeper webhook retries & partner-run routing policy
messages:
From: Ava Mendes <ava@gatekeepersys.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@gatekeepersys.com, DevOps Team <devops@gatekeepersys.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration support — intermittent webhook failures

Hi Grace,

We're seeing a spike of intermittent 5xx responses for inbound webhooks to Redwood's /hooks/ingest endpoint originating from our customers. Failures started on Oct 7 after we enabled a backlog re-play job; roughly ~8-12% of deliveries are now getting 502/504 and not being retried successfully. We've attached a short sample of the error traces (gatekeeper_error_log_20261007.txt).

Immediate ask: can you confirm the following so we can coordinate on-call routing and retries?
- What routing policy is applied when the hosted pool shows transient overload? (do requests get routed to a lower-tier model or dropped?)
- Can Redwood enable a temporary retry-window/backoff recommendation on your side while we throttle replay?
- We need a short bridge (30m) with your infra on-call to share traces and agree a short mitigation.

Our logs show consistent timing around 14:00-16:00 UTC. We're ready to join a bridge today.

Thanks,
Ava Mendes
Partner Success Manager, Gatekeeper Systems
attachments: gatekeeper_error_log_20261007.txt
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Integration support — intermittent webhook failures

Team — forwarding Gatekeeper's report. Short version: partner replay job is overloading our ingest path for some customers and Gatekeeper needs a temporary routing/retry plan plus a bridge.

Immediate proposed steps (please ack and add):
1) Jonas: can you check whether BridgeRouter sent this traffic to a fallback pool (hosted vs dedicated) and whether that caused a content-negotiation failure? We need an initial triage within 2 hours.
2) Marissa: coordinate partner comms and offer two bridge windows (15:30 UTC or 16:30 UTC).
3) Laura: pull contract / SLOs for Gatekeeper (any specific SL revisions that modify retry expectations).
4) Sergio: prep our support_matrix_v2.xlsx mapping for partner-run failures -> owner routing.

I'm looping internal on-call but please keep replies concise. I'll confirm a bridge time to Ava as soon as Jonas reports back.

On Fri, 09 Oct 2026 at 11:12 AM Ava Mendes <ava@gatekeepersys.com> wrote:
> (original message attached)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Integration support — intermittent webhook failures

I looked at the ingress traces for Gatekeeper traffic between Oct 7-9. Quick findings:
- A subset of Gatekeeper requests were being routed to the "dedicated-pool-fallback" path due to transient capacity signals. Those fallback handlers are configured to use an older serialization layer for the payload (legacy token header handling) which can drop connections when the payload includes the new compressed headers Gatekeeper added.
- The 502s correlate with a mismatch on Content-Encoding and an immediate timeout at the LB (we see TCP FIN after 8s).

Short mitigations we can do now (low risk):
- Pin Gatekeeper traffic to the hosted stable variant (redwood-latency-stable-v1) for 24 hours. That bypasses the fallback path.
- Temporarily increase LB idle timeout from 8s to 16s for Gatekeeper CIDRs to allow slower upstreams to complete.
- Provide recommended client-side exponential backoff policy (we can draft language).

I attached the support matrix draft (support_matrix_v2.xlsx) and will stand by for the bridge. If we agree on pinning traffic, I can push a scoped routing override now.

Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: support_matrix_v2.xlsx
From: Ava Mendes <ava@gatekeepersys.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@gatekeepersys.com>, support@gatekeepersys.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration support — intermittent webhook failures

Thanks, Grace & Jonas — that analysis matches what we see. We're comfortable with the temporary pin to redwood-latency-stable-v1 and the LB timeout increase.

Proposed next steps from Gatekeeper side:
- We'll throttle the backlog replays to 1/10th of the current rate for the next 6 hours.
- We'll apply a client retry policy that does up to 3 retries with jitter and initial backoff 500ms; we can push a patch that adds a 50ms client-side jitter to reduce bursts (attachment: gatekeeper_retry_patch.diff).
- We can join a 30-minute bridge at 16:30 UTC today to confirm traces and watch error rates.

Can you put the routing pin in place now and confirm when the LB timeout is adjusted?

Ava
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Mendes <ava@gatekeepersys.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration support — intermittent webhook failures — action items and closure

Ava — quick update and closure notes after bridge today:

What we did
- Pin applied: redwood-latency-stable-v1 routing override scoped to Gatekeeper CIDRs (applied 2026-10-09T16:45:00Z).
- LB idle timeout increased to 16s for the same CIDR range (applied 2026-10-09T16:50:00Z).
- Gatekeeper reduced replay rate and deployed gatekeeper_retry_patch.diff on Oct 9 at 17:10 UTC.

Outcome
- Error rate for Gatekeeper deliveries dropped from ~10% to ~0.6% in 3 hours post-mitigation.
- No further regressions observed; ticket GP-2345 will track a follow-up to harden serializer compatibility.

Action items (owners)
- Redwood SRE (Jonas): implement a permanent detection rule to avoid routing to legacy-serializer fallback for payloads with Content-Encoding header (due 2026-10-23).
- Partnerships (Marissa): update partner runbook and pin policy docs; share with Gatekeeper by 2026-10-16 (drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Gatekeeper-Runbooks).
- Legal/Contracts (Laura): confirm if retry obligations in the contract require amendment; advise by 2026-10-20.

Thanks everyone — closing this thread for now. If Gatekeeper sees anything new, please reopen or file GP-2345.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Partnerships, Redwood Inference
